- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.5) — especially after recent spikes — and adjust downward if sentiment drops below 0.4.
- Underestimate prices during bearish sentiment (sentiment < 0.3) — particularly when historical price trend is rising — and add a small upward bias.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., >75% from prior day) — reduce forecast by 5–10% for the next 3–5 days.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 2–5% per day until convergence.
- Lagged bias: if forecast is >10% above true outcome 3–5 days prior, reduce by 3–5% for next 3–7 days.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts tend to overestimate in high-sentiment periods — apply 2–5% downward correction if sentiment > 0.6 over last 7 days.
- Avoid “sentiment echo” — if sentiment is rising but price is falling, reduce forecast by 3–5% to avoid overcorrection.
